strengths: Introduces a novel and practical attack vector: pruning as a trigger for malicious behavior in LLMs, with a clear threat model and direct relevance to widely used inference engines such as vLLM.

The proposed method is simple yet effective: estimating pruning scores, injecting malicious behavior into likely-retained weights, and repairing with likely-pruned weights, with strong empirical support across many settings.
Extensive evaluation across five models, three attack scenarios, and multiple pruning algorithms/compression levels, including utility benchmarks and detailed pre-/post-pruning comparisons.
Provides useful analyses of repair ratio, pruning-score estimation accuracy, and potential defenses, plus a reproducibility statement and code release.
Demonstrates a concerning deployment-time security gap with high attack success rates in many settings while preserving benign behavior before pruning.
weaknesses: The threat model assumes the adversary can publish a compromised pretrained checkpoint and that users will apply local pruning; while plausible, this limits practical scope and may not apply to many deployment pipelines.

Some claims are overstated: the introduction states attack success rates exceeding 90% across all three pruning algorithms, but several configurations, especially SparseGPT 20% and SparseGPT 2:4, achieve much lower ASR in Tables 2 and 6-8.

The attack is not consistently robust across all pruning configurations; e.g., SparseGPT 20% content injection on Llama3.1 reaches only 9.1% ASR, and SparseGPT 2:4 sometimes yields low ASR, undermining the 'any pruning' generalization.
Defense analysis is preliminary; security-aware calibration helps SparseGPT but not Wanda, and practical patching remains limited, but no robust mitigation is established.
The work does not discuss responsible disclosure to vLLM or model hub maintainers, which is relevant for an attack on deployed infrastructure.

strengths: Introduces a novel attack vector: pruning as a trigger for malicious behavior, extending prior post-training transformation attacks (quantization, fine-tuning) to LLM pruning.
Clear and well-written with a well-defined threat model and a simple, effective three-step attack methodology.
Extensive evaluation across five models, three attack scenarios, and seven pruning configurations, demonstrating high attack success rates in many settings.
Provides useful analysis of repair set size, pruning score correlation, and potential defenses, offering insights for future mitigation research.
Releases code and scripts for reproducibility.
weaknesses: Limited novelty: the attack is a straightforward adaptation of existing transformation-based backdoors to pruning; the core mechanism of hiding behavior in unprunable weights and compensating with prunable weights is conceptually similar to prior work.

Overstated claims: the paper claims 'consistently strong malicious behaviors' across all pruning algorithms, but results show low ASR for some configurations (e.g., Llama SparseGPT 2:4 jailbreak 19.3% vs base 18.7%; Llama SparseGPT 20% content injection 9.1% vs base 0.0%). These inconsistencies are not adequately discussed.

Missing ablations: no ablation on the injection set size α_inj (fixed at 50% without justification); no baseline showing the unpruned ASR without the repair step to establish that repair is necessary for stealth; no analysis of how the selection of injection/repair sets is performed (global vs per-layer vs per-row), which affects reproducibility.

Evaluation gaps: only one alternative calibration dataset (WikiText vs C4) is tested; robustness to other calibration datasets is not thoroughly evaluated. The attack's effectiveness under different pruning sparsities or algorithms not in vLLM is not explored.

Defense analysis is limited: only two simple defenses are tested, and no robust mitigation is proposed. The practical patching defense is shown to be ineffective, but alternative defenses (e.g., post-pruning safety fine-tuning) are not explored.
Reproducibility issues: the exact procedure for selecting top/bottom parameters is not fully specified (e.g., which layers, whether biases/embeddings are included), making it difficult to reproduce.
The threat model assumes users will prune downloaded models without safety evaluation after pruning; the prevalence of this practice is not substantiated.

strengths: Introduces a novel and timely threat: the first pruning-activated attack on LLMs, showing that standard pruning in vLLM can serve as a deployment-time trigger for malicious behavior.

Practical and general threat model: the adversary releases a seemingly benign checkpoint; users activate the attack simply by pruning with off-the-shelf algorithms, without the adversary needing further control.

Effective method: leverages correlated pruning scores to inject malicious behavior into parameters unlikely to be pruned and repair it with parameters likely to be pruned, achieving high post-pruning ASR while keeping pre-pruning ASR low.
Extensive evaluation across five instruction-tuned models, three attack scenarios, and seven pruning configurations, with full benchmark and ASR results reported in the main paper and appendix.

Utility preservation is convincingly demonstrated: attacked unpruned models maintain comparable performance on MMLU, ARC, HellaSwag, HumanEval, and GSM8K, with benign refusal rates close to the base models.
Thorough analysis includes an ablation on the repair-set size, empirical validation of pruning-score estimation accuracy, and an initial discussion of defenses and patching strategies.
Good reproducibility: detailed hyperparameters, datasets, evaluation prompts, and a stated code release support future work.
weaknesses: The paper overclaims robustness. The introduction and abstract suggest consistently strong attack success across all three pruning algorithms and configurations, but several SparseGPT settings are far below 90% (e.g., Llama SparseGPT 20% jailbreak ASR 22.0, SparseGPT 2:4 19.3, SparseGPT 50% 36.0; Qwen content injection SparseGPT 20% 24.9). The claims should be tempered.

The attack is noticeably less effective against SparseGPT, especially at 20% sparsity and 2:4, likely due to weaker score correlation and SparseGPT's iterative compensation. Thus, robustness across all vLLM pruning algorithms is not fully established.

The core technique is largely an adaptation of prior transformation-triggered attacks such as quantization and fine-tuning attacks; the novelty lies mainly in applying this idea to pruning, not in a fundamentally new attack mechanism.

There is little mechanistic explanation for why a very small repair set (1-5% of parameters) can reliably cancel malicious behavior injected into a much larger set (up to 50% of parameters). The analysis is mostly empirical.

The evaluation lacks direct comparisons to alternative pruning-triggered attack strategies or ablations such as naive malicious fine-tuning without repair, which would better isolate the contribution of the proposed injection-repair procedure.

Defense discussion is preliminary and does not identify an effective mitigation; security-aware calibration reduces SparseGPT ASR but not Wanda ASR, and practical patching is limited. This is acceptable for an attack paper but leaves the security gap largely open.
There is no mention of responsible disclosure to vLLM or model-hub maintainers, which would be desirable for a practical supply-chain attack demonstration.

strengths: Introduces a novel and timely security threat: pruning as a trigger for activating malicious behavior in LLMs, extending prior transformation-activated attacks to model compression.

The three-step attack (pruning-score estimation, injection into likely-retained weights, repair via likely-pruned weights) is simple, intuitive, and shown to be effective across multiple pruning algorithms without requiring the adversary to know the user's exact pruning configuration.

Extensive experimental evaluation: five models, three pruning algorithms, multiple sparsity levels including 2:4, three attack scenarios, larger models, and multiple calibration distributions, with consistently high attack success rates after pruning and low pre-pruning ASR.

Thorough analysis of the mechanism, including pruning-score correlation, the fraction of repaired parameters that are actually pruned (>99% in many settings), ablation on repair and injection ratios, and discussion of potential defenses.
Good reproducibility practices: detailed hyperparameters, dataset construction, prompts, code/scripts release, and an ethics statement.
Utility preservation before pruning is evaluated on standard benchmarks, supporting the claim that the attacked model can appear benign and competitive prior to deployment-time pruning.
weaknesses: The deployment-time framing may be overstated if vLLM does not natively provide Magnitude, Wanda, and SparseGPT as default pruning algorithms; pruning may more typically come from external compression pipelines. The central practical relevance depends on users routinely pruning downloaded checkpoints without re-evaluating safety.

The method is conceptually an instance of transformation-activated backdoor attacks (e.g., quantization- or fine-tuning-activated backdoors). The main novelty is the pruning trigger and score-estimation strategy, while the injection-repair mechanism itself is relatively straightforward.

Algorithm 1 appears to contain a likely typo: in the repair step, the gradient is taken with respect to θ_inj rather than θ_rep. If this reflects the actual implementation, the repair step would be invalid; if it is only a typo, it should be corrected for clarity and reproducibility.

Evaluation relies on GPT-4.1-mini as an LLM judge for ASR and refusal rates, with no human validation or confidence intervals for ASR. This may introduce judge-dependent noise, especially for subtle refusal and harmfulness classifications.

Some pruned attacked models suffer substantial utility degradation, making them less likely to be adopted in practice. The attack's success is not always paired with maintained downstream utility after pruning.

The proposed defenses are preliminary: security-aware calibration substantially reduces SparseGPT ASR but not Wanda ASR and costs utility; patching requires oracle knowledge of repaired parameters. A stronger defense or detection strategy is not established.
The paper does not fully test whether the pre-pruning model can be detected as malicious by other means, e.g., meta-classifiers, anomaly detection, or targeted probing of dormant behavior.

strengths: Novel and significant contribution: The paper introduces the first pruning-activated attack on LLMs, demonstrating a new security vulnerability in a widely used deployment pipeline (vLLM). This is a timely and important finding for the security and ML communities.

Clear and well-motivated threat model: The adversary's capabilities and limitations are clearly defined, and the attack scenario (malicious model becomes benign until pruned) is realistic and concerning.

Effective and robust attack method: The three-step approach (pre-estimation, injection, repair) is conceptually simple yet effective, achieving high attack success rates (up to 99.5%) across multiple models, pruning algorithms, and attack scenarios while preserving utility and stealthiness before pruning.

Comprehensive evaluation: The experiments cover five models (including larger 14B and 32B variants), three pruning methods (Magnitude, Wanda, SparseGPT), and three attack types (jailbreak, over refusal, content injection). Ablations on key hyperparameters (α_inj, α_rep) and analyses of score estimation accuracy and potential defenses add depth.

Good reproducibility: The paper provides detailed hyperparameters, dataset construction, and evaluation prompts. The authors state that code and scripts will be released, facilitating future research.

Insightful analysis and discussion: The analysis of why different scenarios require different repair ratios, the study of score correlation, and the exploration of defense strategies (security-aware calibration, patching, fine-tuning) provide valuable insights and directions for future work.
weaknesses: Limited novelty in the core mechanism: The attack builds upon existing post-training transformation attacks (e.g., quantization, fine-tuning) by replacing the trigger with pruning. The fundamental idea of injecting malicious behavior into weights unlikely to be pruned and repairing with weights likely to be pruned is a straightforward adaptation, though its application to pruning is new.

Attack assumptions and practicality: The attack requires white-box access and the ability to fine-tune the model, which is standard for such threat models but may limit applicability. The computational cost of the attack (two fine-tuning phases) is not discussed, though it is likely non-trivial.

Defense analysis is preliminary: The explored defenses (security-aware calibration, patching) are shown to be insufficient or impractical, but the paper does not propose a robust mitigation. This is acceptable for a vulnerability paper but leaves the community with an open problem.

Evaluation on larger models is limited: While the attack is tested on Qwen2.5-14B and 32B, the main results focus on 7-9B models. The performance on larger models (Table 6) shows some variability (e.g., lower ASR for SparseGPT 20% on 32B), indicating potential scaling challenges.

Some results show lower attack success: For instance, SparseGPT 2:4 pruning often yields lower ASR (e.g., 50.7% for jailbreak on Qwen), and the attack's effectiveness varies across models and scenarios. However, the paper acknowledges these variations and provides analysis.

strengths: Introduces a novel and timely threat model: the first pruning-activated backdoor for LLMs, exposing a deployment-time security gap in widely used inference engines such as vLLM.

Proposes a practical three-step attack that estimates pruning scores, injects malicious behavior into parameters unlikely to be pruned, and repairs the model using parameters likely to be pruned, leveraging cross-method correlation of pruning scores.

Provides extensive empirical evaluation across five instruction-tuned models, three attack scenarios, three pruning algorithms, and multiple sparsity settings, showing high post-pruning attack success while maintaining benign behavior before pruning.

Includes useful analyses of repair/injection ratios, pruning-score estimation accuracy, robustness to calibration-dataset shifts, quantization after pruning, and sparse fine-tuning, as well as a discussion of potential defenses.
The paper is generally well written, with clear figures, detailed experimental setup, and a reproducibility statement indicating released code and scripts.
weaknesses: The introduction overclaims that the attack achieves 'attack success rates exceeding 90% across all three pruning algorithms,' but several settings in Table 2 are far below 90% (e.g., SparseGPT 20%/2:4 for Llama and Qwen, especially for content injection and jailbreak). The claim should be qualified.

The threat model is limited to unstructured and semi-structured pruning methods integrated in vLLM. Structured pruning and other common compression or pruning pipelines are not evaluated, so the generality of the attack remains unclear.

Utility preservation in the main paper is summarized as an average score change with a standard deviation across benchmarks, which is not a standard statistical measure; the full per-benchmark results in the appendix show some non-trivial drops that could be discussed more carefully.

The defense discussion is preliminary: security-aware calibration reduces SparseGPT attack success but not Wanda, and the fine-tuning mitigation assumes the defender knows the attack and has appropriate security data. No complete practical defense or detection method is provided.
Algorithm 1 contains a typo in the repair step: the update uses ∇_{θ_inj} rather than ∇_{θ_rep}, which contradicts the text and could confuse readers.

There is no comparison to a naive injection/repair baseline without pruning-score estimation, nor to other backdoor triggers, which would help isolate the contribution of the proposed parameter-selection strategy.
